rationale: C08 is the closest because it shares the formulation “subject to valid existing rights,” followed by an operative disposition of specifically described land, a legal-description block, and an acreage statement. C07 likewise contains surveyed land descriptions and an aggregate-acreage statement, while C13 reproduces the same monument material as C08 despite its inconsistent title. These similarities are conventional land-order language and formatting, however. None of the candidates contains the child’s distinctive machinery of opening land to mining-law location and entry, delaying the status change until 10:00 a.m. on the thirty-fifth day, and then making the land subject to mining-law disposal. The displayed evidence therefore does not establish a concrete, material drafting-template relationship.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Subject to valid existing rights ... the following-described land is hereby opened to location and entry under the mining laws
shared_material.parent_excerpt: subject to valid existing rights, the following-described tract of land in New Mexico is hereby added to and reserved as a part of the Aztec Ruins National Monument
shared_material.explanation: C08 shares the opening qualification and the syntax introducing a legally described tract, but applies opposite and materially different land-status machinery.

shared_material.explanation: C07 shares the public-land survey and acreage format, which is routine in land directives and does not show reuse of the operative mining provisions.
